results.construction: Points mode, range [-6,6]: tap -3 and 3. Both are whole numbers within the range, 2 targets (within 1–4).

predicates.why: A student who excludes numerator zeroes would mark x=1 instead of ±3, so the marks would be {1}. That does fire extra-values, because 1 is not in the answer set. But it would also fire missed-values, and extra-values fires on any stray mark, such as a sign error or a guessed value. It is not specific to this misconception, so the diagnosis is not safe.

A student who finds only the positive root marks {3} and leaves out -3. That is a strict subset of the answer set, with no extra marks, so missed-values fires. This is the typical result of the one-root-only-denominator error for x²=9.

results.construction: Points mode, range [-6,6]: tap x=-2 and x=2 (denominator x^2-4=0). Both are whole numbers inside the range, 2 targets.

predicates.why: A student who finds only the positive root marks {2} and omits -2. Part of the answer set is unmarked, so the predicate fires, and this is the one-root-only error.
A student who sets the numerator to zero marks x=-1, which is not in the answer set, so the predicate fires. It may also fire with missed-values, but extra-values fits this misconception.
